julie: Heads-up: onboarding Halo-21B (Llama-ish arch but uses Qwen tokenizer) into our llama runtime. Conversion + int4 quant done; shortbench ok but long-context QA and summarization show weird directive insertion and occasional token boundary splits.

mark: can you paste repro and what you saw?

julie: short repro below. convert qwen->llama with autodetect heads + token-map normalize-zwj; quantize with int4 calib=150k pack-order=chunked. Serve on dedicated dev pool. Results: for contexts >1800 tokens, model sometimes injects "See Appendix" style fragments and occasionally breaks a word mid-token. Float32 fine.

julie: ```bash
python convert_qwen_to_llama.py --in halo21b.qwen --out halo21b.llama --autodetect-heads --token-map normalize-zwj
python quantize.py --model halo21b.llama --dtype int4 --calib 150000 --pack-order chunked
redwood serve --model halo21b.int4 --profile long-summarize
```

yara: paste a minimal example (float vs int4) if you have it.

julie: float32: "The team recommends a phased rollout starting Q1 with canary nodes."

int4: "The team recommends a phased rollout starting Q1 with canary nodes.
Note: see Appendix C for migration steps."

julie: also saw token split: float32 returns "namespaces"; int4 returns "name
spaces" (split in the middle with newline).

mark: interesting — two likely issues: (1) rotary/head layout mismatch causing KV cache phase swaps over long context; (2) embedding/token-table row-shift due to pack stride/padding. Which one reproduces on quant-sim?

julie: ran fake-quant (dequant sim) and the directive insertion reproduces with pack-order=chunked. If I change pack-order to contiguous the issue disappears in sim. Also, disabling runtime head-scale flag (--rotary-head-scale=off) reduces the frequency of directive insertion but doesn't fully fix token splits.

yara: that suggests packer layout + head-scale interactions. Maybe chunked packing interleaves head blocks differently and runtime's head-scale map assumes contiguous ordering. The token split could be an unrelated packing stride/padding bug in embedding table.

devops-bot: artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-dev/model-artifacts/halo21b/debug-pack/ (sha256: deadbeef).

mark: can you run per-head rotary-base diff test? small snippet: load orig rotary bases and deserialized ones and compute max abs diff per head. If certain head groups show large diffs that's our smoking gun.

julie: ran it. With chunked pack-order diffs spike on heads [8,9,24,25]; with contiguous diffs ~1e-9 across the board. Embedding row-hash test also shows mismatches at indices multiple of 32 (pack stride).

yara: remediation ideas: (A) have the packer write explicit header metadata (head_layout, pack_stride) + crc for rotary and embedding tables so runtime can validate & remap on load; (B) change packer default to runtime-canonical contiguous layout and re-pack existing artifacts; (C) add conversion CI smoke tests: per-head rotary alignment + per-row embedding hash roundtrip.

mark: +1 to header metadata (low-risk) + smoke tests in CI. We'll want a migration plan to re-pack any artifacts converted in the last 30 days. Also add a short long-context eval (100 docs) to conversion smoke so we catch these patterns earlier.

julie: I'll open RI-2301 with artifacts and proposed patch to add header {"head_layout":"chunked","pack_stride":32,"crc_rotary":"...","crc_embed_rows":"..."}. Tagging eng-runtime and tokenizers.

ci-bot: build 4801 triggered: tests/convert::halo-pack-header-check started.

yara: once CI green, re-run long-summarize eval on the repacked int4 and fake-quant artifacts. If header+remap fixes both directive insertion and token-split we can schedule a small backfill.

julie: noted. I'll queue overnight runs after CI. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
